analysis: Examined the MediaIngest.swift change: inline-video data-URI header admission moves from two case-insensitive comparisons to a lowercased Set lookup. It adds data:video/x-m4v;base64 and data:video/mov;base64. The body still goes through dataFromDataURI with maxMediaDecodedBytes, then MemoryBackedVideoAsset. The threat-model text says that asset sniffs the container from the bytes, with forbidAll reference restrictions, memory-backed ranges and no temp file, so the extra labels widen only the accepted label strings, not the parser or the file-based plaintext exposure addressed by T-050. The existing duration, frame-pixel, count and aggregate caps are described as unchanged. No file-write or URL path was introduced in the visible patch (T-050 detection hint not triggered). Header matching is exact on the lowercased prefix before the comma, so parameters such as charset are not admitted, which is a stricter-than-needed form of matching. The docs/threat-model.yaml change (line 1969-1970) only updates T-050's prose to match the code. Its YAML structure is intact in the visible head excerpts, and it does not weaken any mitigation. The libs/mlx-swift-lm submodule pointer moved from 7bed821 to 6aef0a5, and the submodule contents are not supplied. That is a coverage limit: I cannot verify whether MemoryBackedVideoAsset, UserInput or MediaProcessing changed, including container sniffing, byte-range serving, reference restrictions or cancellation. T-050 and TB-007 depend on those. The submodule bump most plausibly supports the new MIME labels, but this is unverified, so a deeper review of the submodule diff is warranted. No findings are reported on the supplied evidence.
